name: Frontal Lobe
summary: The largest lobe, occupying about one-third of the cortical surface. Home to executive functions, personality, speech production, and voluntary motor control.

connections.note: Links motor planning with spatial awareness.
Connects Broca's area to Wernicke's area for language.

facts.text: The prefrontal cortex doesn't fully mature until around age 25, which helps explain why teenagers often struggle with impulse control and long-term planning.
Damage to Broca's area causes expressive aphasia — understanding language perfectly but being unable to produce fluent speech.

detailedDescription: The frontal lobe's anterior portion is the prefrontal cortex (PFC) — the seat of executive functions. The dorsolateral PFC handles working memory, planning, and cognitive flexibility. The ventromedial PFC manages emotional regulation, risk assessment, and empathy. The orbitofrontal cortex processes reward and decision-making. The precentral gyrus at the rear contains the primary motor cortex — a strip running ear-to-ear where each point controls a specific muscle group (motor homunculus).
